messages.author: 328da6b8437ee6df
messages.subject: Shiny server and pander
parts:
Dear RStudio team,

Congratulations, Shiny server may be one of the best things that have happened to R since R.

Nevertheless, deploying an application (http://glimmer.rstudio.com/grserrano/idts/) to hosted shiny server I almost went mad: he app was running properly in my Mac, but an error raised when I ran it in the server. I've narrowed down the problem to loading pander package. If I don't do library(pander) everything works fine, but when loaded, there's a conflict with p() function which stops/freezes the app running in the server. I've solved de problem as I don't need pander in this case, but I think it's very useful for report generation.

Thanks for your work,

Gregorio R. Serrano

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server and pander
parts:
Did your app directly call to the p() function anywhere? If so, one thing you could do is use shiny::p(), to tell it to use the shiny version of p().


-Winston

Hi.

It doesn't call nor shiny::p() nor pander::p(), it calls pandoc.table(). I solved the problem the reverse way, using pander::pandoc.table().

Thanks,
Gregorio
